key_facts: Plaintiff has an established prior employment history with Randstad. Defendant Randstad US, LLC (operating as Randstad General Staffing and, within client facilities, as Randstad Inhouse Services) is a Delaware LLC and the primary Randstad operating entity for general staffing placements in California; 'Randstad General Staffing' and 'Randstad Inhouse Services' are trade names and division brands, not separate legal entities. Defendant RK Logistics Group, Inc. is a California corporation (incorporated April 23, 2004, HQ: 47020 Kato Road, Fremont, CA 94538) — a 3PL company specializing in semiconductor, EV, and high-tech logistics with multiple Bay Area facilities. Randstad Inhouse Services embeds a dedicated site manager within the RK Logistics facility. On June 30, 2026, Plaintiff submitted an employment application via the Indeed platform for the position of 'Class C Driver - Bobtail (Mon-Fri 2:30pm-11:00pm)' listed by RK Logistics Group, Inc. at its Newark, CA facility. RK Logistics sent Plaintiff an automated SMS acknowledgment at 8:26 PM on June 30 from +1 (762) 795-5146: 'Thanks for your interest in RK Logistics Group, Inc jobs.' The following morning, July 1, 2026 at 8:08 AM, Randstad recruiter Dishon Bryant texted Plaintiff from +1 (609) 901-1636: 'Hi Brendan, This is Dishon with Randstad. I'm contacting you regarding the class C driver position you applied for at RK Logistics. Give me a call when you get a chance.' This message establishes the direct nexus between Plaintiff's Indeed application and Randstad's inhouse staffing pipeline: Randstad's outreach came within approximately 12 hours of the Indeed application. On July 2, 2026, Dishon Bryant followed up by text, providing the identity and contact number of the embedded RK Logistics site manager: 'Site Manger / Danyea Watkins -5106955468' — the same Danyea Watkins (danyea.watkins@randstadusa.com; 510-695-5468) who, five days later, emailed Plaintiff the MVR form confirming the CDL commercial driving placement. The Bryant-to-Watkins text chain documents the complete pre-onboarding pipeline: Plaintiff's June 30 Indeed application to RK Logistics triggered Randstad's recruiter outreach within hours; Randstad then referred Plaintiff to the embedded RK Logistics site manager; and five days later the site manager completed onboarding with the MVR form. On July 7, 2026, Randstad sent Plaintiff a formal notification: 'Your employee status has changed to Rehired' — re-onboarding him into Randstad's operations with self-service portal access at workplace.randstad.com and weekly paycheck processing. That same afternoon, at 2:45 PM, RIS Site Manager II Danyea Watkins (danyea.watkins@randstadusa.com; 510-695-5468) — operating inside the RK Logistics Fremont facility — emailed Plaintiff requesting completion of an MVR (Motor Vehicle Record) form, confirming Plaintiff was being placed in a CDL commercial driving role. At 6:22 PM on July 7, 2026, Randstad submitted a background check request through vendor InfoMart LLC (Order No. 15780719) for the 'Randstad App' placement. The InfoMart report header confirms: Billing Code: RK LOGISTICS; Business Unit: RIS RK Logistics Fremont; Client Package: RK Logistics — strongly supporting that RK Logistics was the billing client and participated in or controlled relevant screening-package criteria; access logs and decision records are still needed to establish which RK/Randstad actor actually viewed or used the registry information. The report's Decision Date is July 13, 2026 and its overall status is 'NEEDS APPROVAL, PER CLIENT CRITERIA.' On July 13, 2026 at 1:31 PM, InfoMart sent Plaintiff a 'Notice to Consumer for Employment Purposes' pursuant to FCRA §607(b) (15 U.S.C. §1681e(b)), informing him that InfoMart is 'reporting criminal or other public record information that may be adverse' to Randstad; dispute address: P.O. Box 2209, Alpharetta, GA 30023. The InfoMart report itself — now in Plaintiff's possession — confirms: (1) criminal history searched across seven jurisdictions: Fresno County CA, San Joaquin County CA, Santa Clara County CA, Stanislaus County CA, Clark County NV, State of New York, and Sheridan County WY — all returned 'No Record'; (2) federal criminal history (National Federal): 'No Record'; (3) OFAC Watch List: 'No name match found'; (4) OIG Exclusions List: 'not found'; (5) GSA Procurement Exclusion: 'not found'; (6) National Criminal Search / Sex Offender: 'Information Found' — jurisdiction: County: Sex Offender, State: California — Result: 'Record' — Name on file: Newanforbi, Brendan Ngehsi — and the report's conclusion: 'Subject is a registered Sex Offender in California.' The California Sex Offender Registry is therefore confirmed as the sole basis for the 'NEEDS APPROVAL' flag. This is not a case pled on information and belief — Plaintiff now holds the actual InfoMart report showing every criminal search returned clear, with the registry listing as the only adverse item. Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E) categorically prohibits the use of registry information 'for purposes relating to ... Employment.' No exception applies to a CDL commercial driving placement. On July 15, 2026, Randstad terminated Plaintiff's employment two business days after InfoMart's July 13 'Notice to Consumer for Employment Purposes.' The FCRA itself does not impose a fixed five-business-day waiting period. Moreover, InfoMart's wording appears consistent with a CRA-side public-record notice under 15 U.S.C. §1681k; the key employer-side question is whether Randstad separately provided the report and summary of rights required by §1681b(b)(3)(A) before adverse action, subject to any applicable transportation-applicant exception. The termination also occurred while the InfoMart result remained 'NEEDS APPROVAL, PER CLIENT CRITERIA.' On July 20, 2026, Plaintiff sent Pre-Filing Demand Letters to both Randstad (privacyofficer@randstad.com, cc: call.center@, rus-privacy@, hrsupport@, complianceofficer@randstadusa.com) and RK Logistics Group, Inc. (info@rklogisticsgroup.com, cc: peter.odonnell@, nikki.michaux@rklogisticsgroup.com), each demanding $85,000 in settlement with a response deadline of 5:00 PM Pacific Time on August 2, 2026, transmitting as an exhibit a verified Complaint for Damages executed the same day naming both entities and DOES 1-20, filed for Alameda Superior Court (venue proper under CCP §§395(a), 395.5 — the RK Logistics Fremont facility where Plaintiff was assigned and where the adverse decision was made and implemented). This is the fifth matter in the portfolio asserting PC §290.46(j) violations by an employer using registry information for employment purposes (Matters 22, 25, 26, 27 — Matter 23 is excluded from this count because Macy's completed the hire without any adverse action; see Matter 23).

damages: PC §290.46(j)(4)(A) permits actual damages; an additional amount determined by the trier of fact not exceeding three times actual damages and not less than $250; attorney's fees; and exemplary damages or a civil penalty not exceeding $25,000. It does NOT create an automatic $25,000 floor. ICRAA §1786.50, if proven and not classwide, separately provides actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater, plus costs/fees and potentially punitive damages for grossly negligent or willful violations. Because Plaintiff remains pro se, his own litigation time should not be modeled as already-accrued recoverable attorney fees. Matter 27's principal valuation drivers are any documented lost wages from an operative rehire/placement, the registry-source evidence, emotional distress, FCRA/ICRAA exposure actually supported by the notice record, and punitive/civil-penalty exposure if causation and willfulness are established.
risk: Strong on source proof but still causation- and actor-dependent. Plaintiff holds InfoMart Order No. 15780719: every criminal-court/federal search is clear and the California sex-offender result is the sole adverse hit. The RK-branded Billing Code, Business Unit, Client Package, and 'NEEDS APPROVAL, PER CLIENT CRITERIA' fields strongly support RK participation in screening criteria, but do not by themselves prove which RK or Randstad actor viewed or used the registry information. Randstad is the more direct §290.46 defendant because it ordered/received the screen and implemented the July 15 termination; RK's exposure turns heavily on portal/access logs, criteria configuration, and decision communications. The contemporaneous MVR email supplies a real competing causation theory and must be tested rather than dismissed as pretext by assumption. FCRA analysis also needs correction: the July 13 InfoMart notice may be a CRA public-record notice under §1681k, not Randstad's employer-side pre-adverse package, and federal law does not create a fixed five-business-day waiting period. Determine whether Randstad separately provided the report and summary of rights required by §1681b(b)(3)(A), and test any transportation-applicant exception. Tameny is strongest against Randstad if the rehire created an employment relationship; RK's employer/joint-employer status remains contested. The two-defendant structure remains strategically useful because cross-blame may generate admissions.
